inputs_used: Orchestrator brief for stage 01 (title, angle, must-includes, overlap split)

payload.title: Australian Wedding Ceremony Script With the Legal Wording
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their thirties planning a wedding with a six-figure AUD budget, who will either marry legally in Australia (often before or after a celebration abroad) and now need to know exactly what their celebrant must say, which lines they can change, and how to write a full ceremony around the legal words.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning the wider wedding (venue, travel, vendors) around the legal ceremony: one click from the closing line to /wonderland-concierge (UTM-tagged).
payload.angle: The one page that puts the Marriage Act 1961 words an Australian ceremony needs, the s46 monitum and the s45 vows, quoted exactly from the official legislation, inside a full original ceremony script, with every line marked legally required or optional. It answers 'what does a celebrant legally have to say in Australia?' directly, where page-one results give generic or US-style scripts with no legal wording or paraphrase it without a source.
must_include: What the law requires in an Australian ceremony, from official sources only (legislation.gov.au Marriage Act 1961 and the Attorney-General's Department): an authorised celebrant physically present; two witnesses over 18 (only if the source states it); the s46 monitum; the s45 vows; marriage certificates signed and the celebrant lodging the registration. Cite each source at the claim and mark every point [[VERIFY]] until the source pack confirms it. Legal points framed as general information as at November 2026.
The legal words quoted exactly as the Act states them (s46 monitum, s45(2) vows including 'or words to that effect'), visually set apart so couples can copy them, with the section number beside each.

A full original ceremony script in order: welcome, the monitum, a reading, vows (legal words then personal vows), ring exchange, declaration, signing of the certificates, presentation of the couple. Each line or block labelled 'Legally required' or 'Optional'. Original wording only.

Personal vows alongside the legal words: explain 'or words to that effect' in plain terms and tell couples to confirm any changed wording with their celebrant. Link /expert-advice/short-wedding-vows for vow examples rather than repeating them.

A short script variant: the legally required core only, for a quick legal ceremony (for example before celebrating abroad). No timings stated as fact; link /expert-advice/how-long-is-a-wedding-ceremony.

A religious minister's ceremony: only what s45(1) states (a minister of a recognised denomination may use the form of their religious body) and whether the monitum applies, quoted from the Act; nothing beyond it.

Marrying overseas: an Australian celebrant can't solemnise a legal marriage overseas [[VERIFY: AGD source]]; the common path is the legal ceremony at home and a symbolic ceremony abroad, linking /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony.

FAQ (4 to 6 questions), led by 'What does a celebrant legally have to say in Australia?', plus: can we change the legal vows, do we need witnesses, does a religious ceremony need the monitum, can our Australian celebrant marry us overseas.

Internal links: /expert-advice/wedding-ceremony-script prominently near the top as the general script hub; /expert-advice/who-can-perform-a-marriage for celebrant authority; /expert-advice/what-happens-in-a-wedding-ceremony; /expert-advice/simple-wedding-ceremony-script; /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage and /expert-advice/sand-ceremony-script only if live at publish time.

Close with one Wedded Advisor line built only from brand-facts lines 19 to 30 (for example one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, planning venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world), with nothing implying the Advisor handles legal paperwork, lodges documents or acts as celebrant.
avoid: Prices, fees, statistics, 'best' claims and any research or methodology talk
Paraphrasing the legal words as if they were the legal text, or any legal wording not traced to legislation.gov.au or the Attorney-General's Department
Any same-sex marriage legal position beyond quoting the Act's current wording
Implying Wedded Wonderland, Wedded Concierge or the Wedded Advisor provides legal advice, celebrant services, Notice of Intended Marriage lodgement or registration
Duplicating short-wedding-vows: no lists of vow examples; this page owns the full AU ceremony script and the legal requirements of the ceremony
Duplicating who-can-perform-a-marriage (celebrant authority detail) and notice-of-intended-marriage (NOIM process): one-line summary plus link
US or UK wording conventions ('officiant' as the main term, 'by the power vested in me' presented as an Australian legal requirement)
Competitor wording, scripts or images; em dashes; US spelling
